qa.question: What kind of card does "a card with X in its text" refer to?
qa.answer:
It refers to a card that contains the specified text or icon in its name, traits, effects, inherited effects, (Rule), digivolve requirements, DNA Digivolve, DigiXros requirements, Burst Digivolve, App Fusion, Link, or Assembly requirements.
For example, "a card with [Knightmon] in its text" would include cards with the name [DarkKnightmon] and cards with the text [Knightmon] in their effects.

qa.question: What positions on the memory gauge does "your opponent has X or more memory" refer to?
qa.answer: It refers to the positions at X and to the right of it on your opponent's side.

qa.question: What does "also" mean?
qa.answer:
“Also” means that the effect given by that effect has the same duration and targets as that effect's previously resolved portion.
For example, in the case of “Until the end of the turn, all of your XX Digimon gain AA. If you have a Tamer, they also gain BB,” all of your XX Digimon gain AA until the end of the turn, and if you have a Tamer, all of your XX Digimon also gain BB until the end of the turn as well.

qa.question: My opponent has 2 Digimon with 3000 DP. Can I activate this card's [When Digivolving] effect to only delete 1 of my opponent's Digimon with 3000 DP?
My opponent has 2 Digimon with 3000 DP. Can I activate this card's [When Digivolving] effect and then not delete any of my opponent's Digimon?
qa.answer: No. You must delete at least 1 of your opponent's Digimon.

qa.question: This card's DP is 12000 and it has gained 1 <Security A. +1> from its own [Your Turn] effect. It performs a security check, and the 1st security check activates another effect, causing this card's DP to drop to 7000 or less. At this time, will it perform the 2nd security check using <Security A. +1>?
qa.answer:
No, the 2nd security check isn't performed.
When this card's DP becomes 7000 or less from the 1st security check, it loses the <Security A. +1> it gained from its own [Your Turn] effect, so the 2nd check isn't performed.

qa.question: I use [Burning Drive] and give 1 of my Digimon +10000 DP. Before processing the part if its effect following "then," if I digivolve my Digimon into this card using this card's Arts Digivolve, can I reference that Digimon's DP to delete an opponent's Digimon?
qa.answer:
No.
You must fully resolve [Burning Drive]'s effect before making the choice to Arts Digivolve or not.

qa.question: I use [Burning Drive] to give 1 of my Digimon +10000 DP. At this time, can I reference the DP of a different Digimon from the one I gave the DP bonus to for the part of the effect after "then"?
What does "isn't affected by [...] effects" mean, exactly?
qa.answer:
This effect prevents a card from being affected by effects.
For example, your Digimon won't suspend if it's chosen for a "suspend 1 of your opponent's Digimon" effect, and its DP won't be reduced by 3000 if it's chosen for a "1 of your opponent's Digimon gets -3000 DP" effect.

qa.question: Can a card that has an "isn't affected by [...] effects" effect be chosen for an effect?
qa.answer:
Yes, it can be chosen.
For example, a Digimon that isn't affected by effects can be chosen for a "suspend 1 of your opponent's Digimon" effect.

qa.question: Can a card that has an "isn't affected by [...] effects" effect be given an effect?
qa.answer:
Yes, it can.
It won't be affected by it, but it can be given an effect.
However, if an effect such as <Security A.> is given to a Digimon that isn't affected by effects, the Digimon won't be considered to have that effect.

qa.question: If a card is affected by an effect, then it later gains an "isn't affected by [...] effects" effect, what happens to the effect that was affecting it?
qa.answer: As soon as it gains the "isn't affected by [...] effects" effect, it will no longer be affected.

qa.question: If a card has an "isn't affected by [...] effects" effect, it gains an effect, then it later loses the "isn't affected by [...] effects" effect, what happens to the effect that it gained?
qa.answer: It will be affected by the effect as soon as it can be affected by effects.

qa.question: A card that has an "isn't affected by [...] effects" effect was given an effect that triggers at a timing such as [When Attacking]. Will the effect trigger if that card later meets the trigger conditions?
qa.answer: If the Digimon isn't affected by effects upon the trigger timing, the effect won't trigger.

comprehensive-0225.title: <Piercing>
comprehensive-0225.text:
16-7. <Piercing>
16-7-1. <Piercing> is a keyword effect that reads "When this Digimon deletes your opponent's Digimon in battle while attacking, it checks security before the attack ends." (For details, refer to 13 "Security Checks")
16-7-2. <Piercing> is a trigger-type effect that triggers and activates when a Digimon with this effect battles an opponent's Digimon and the opponent's Digimon is deleted in battle. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger- Type Effects")
16-7-3. The security check from using <Piercing> is mandatory.
16-7-4. <Piercing> is pending processing that is processed immediately before the transition to the end of attack timing. Therefore, it will trigger simultaneously with effects triggered by the battle, but it is processed before the end of the attack. (Example: If a Digimon with <Piercing> attacks and deletes a Digimon with an [On Deletion] effect in the battle, first the [On Deletion] effect is resolved, then <Piercing> is processed.)
16-7-5. Only 1 security check can be performed during a single attack, even if <Piercing> activates multiple times. However, if the number of cards that can be checked by the attacking Digimon is modified, that number of cards will be checked in a single security check.
16-7-6. If there are no Digimon to perform a security check at the point when <Piercing> is processed, a security check won't be possible.

comprehensive-0242.title: <Raid>
comprehensive-0242.text:
16-23. <Raid>
16-23-1. <Raid> is a keyword effect that can switch the target of attack to the opponent's unsuspended Digimon with the highest DP when a Digimon with this keyword effect attacks.
16-23-2. <Raid> is a trigger-type effect that triggers when a Digimon with this effect attacks. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger-Type Effects")
16-23-3. The processing from <Raid> is optional.
16-23-4. If the opponent has multiple unsuspended Digimon with the highest DP when <Raid> activates, the player that activated the effect chooses a Digimon from among them and the attack target is switched to it.

comprehensive-0258.title: <Progress>
comprehensive-0258.text:
16-39. <Progress>
16-39-1. <Progress> is a keyword effect that reads "this Digimon isn't affected by your opponent's effects while attacking."
16-39-2. <Progress> is a persistent effect. (For details, refer to 15-8-2 "Persistent Effects")
16-39-3. <Progress> will activate while the Digimon with this effect is attacking.

comprehensive-0321.title: <Engage>
comprehensive-0321.text:
16-44. <Engage>
16-44-1. <Engage> is a keyword effect where a Digimon with this effect may attack at the end of your turn.
16-44-2. <Engage> is a trigger-type effect that triggers at the End of Your Turn timing. (For details, refer to 15-8-3 "Trigger-Type Effects")
16-44-3. The processing from <Engage> is optional.
